newsitem.title: CANADA: Sun Media Corp to buy London Free Press.
newsitem.headline: Sun Media Corp to buy London Free Press.

text.p: Sun Media Corp said on Thursday that it signed a letter of intent with the Blackburn Group Inc to purchase the London Free Press Printing Co Ltd and Netmar Inc.

The Free Press is Canada's second-largest independent newspaper and one of the country's oldest dailies. The Free Press, and Netmar, Canada's largest publisher and distributor of weekly shopper publications, were offered for sale on January 29.
"It has long been a dream of ours to bring the London Free Press into our family," said Paul Godfrey, President and Chief Executive Officer of Sun Media.

Details of the letter of intent between BGI and Sun Media will remain confidential during final due diligence and the drafting of a purchase and sale agreement. However, Godfrey indicated both sides would move quickly to close the deal.

The Free Press has daily circulation of approximately 105,000 and Saturday circulation of 135,000 and will make privately-held Sun Media the second-largest daily newspaper group in Canada, based on circulation.

Netmar Inc incorporates 14 shopper publications, four weekly newspapers in Ontario, a group of weekly papers in the Edmonton area and a distribution arm that can reach up to nine million Canadian households. Netmar operates in 25 Canadian cities and is a strong strategic fit, said Godfrey.
As a result of this acquisition, Sun Media will publish 11 dailies, 84 weekly community newspapers and shopping guides and 15 farming and other specialty publications in Canada and the U.S.
